confirmed_weaknesses.weakness: The claim's substantive dependency points are TRUE and source-backed, but it materially misstates the headline number and what the verdict rests on. (1) NUMBER: The aggregate cluster EBITDA/interest coverage computed from the exact fixture feeding the report (handoffs/fixtures/ai_direct_issuer_financials.csv, 11 source-backed issuers; mirrored in handoffs/ai_direct_issuer_financials_20260602.json) is 1.349x (agg EBITDA $2,211,948,000 / agg interest $1,639,629,000) — NOT "near ~1x." More damning, the report's own narration of this figure is internally wrong: scripts/generate_final_burry_report.py:1398-1400 tells the reader "Below ~1 means operations do not cover interest before any principal; this figure is propped by a single issuer (negative ex-CoreWeave)," and burry_verdict.py:179 says the cluster "already runs near 1x coverage at base." At 1.35x the aggregate cluster DOES cover interest with a ~35% buffer; the "below ~1 / do not cover interest" framing is contradicted by the engine's own computed value. (2) WHAT THE VERDICT RESTS ON: The 0.67 confidence does NOT rest on the aggregate ratio. It is derived (burry_verdict.py:249-250, 300) from majority_fragile = (loss_making>=usable/2 OR below_1>=usable/2), which is true because 7 of 11 issuers are loss-making and 7 of 11 are sub-1x → fragility_facts_confidence=0.85, then discounted by bear confidence (~0.605) to 0.67. The aggregate coverage ratio is reported as descriptive color, not a confidence input, so "rests mainly on aggregate coverage near ~1x" mischaracterizes the derivation. (3) "Propped by a single issuer" oversimplifies: removing CoreWeave does flip the aggregate negative (ex-CoreWeave -0.48x, agg EBITDA -$196M — this part is TRUE and stated at burry_verdict.py:271-274,331-334), but CleanSpark (+$667M EBITDA, 58.9x, the only is_loss_making:false issuer), Bitdeer (+$328M), and IREN (+$278M) are also large positive props; the negative ex-CoreWeave result is driven as much by the seven loss-makers as by CoreWeave's singular size. So the claim correctly flags the CoreWeave dependency and negative ex-CoreWeave aggregate (both real and disclosed), but errs on the magnitude ("~1x" vs 1.35x), inherits the report's self-contradictory "below ~1 / do not cover interest" mislabel, and overstates the aggregate ratio as the load-bearing premise.
confirmed_weaknesses.recommendation: Fix both the report narration and the claim wording. confirmed_weaknesses.weakness:
The "3 of 3 first-principles conditions met" rests on a defective third leg: the execution/satellite condition. Two distinct problems compound in forensic_fragility_scorecard.py:124-146 and src/bubble/ingestion/satellite.py:60-65,114-115.

(1) CONFOUNDED PROXY MISLABELED AS FACT. The condition is `share_of_sites_with_no_construction > 50%` (scorecard line 129), where `no_change_sites` counts ONLY the classifier's `no_significant_change` bucket (satellite.py:114-115), defined as all of NDVI/NDBI/BSI deltas being near-zero (`abs < 0.05`, satellite.py:64). But "no Sentinel-2 change between 2023-24 and 2025-26" is NOT equivalent to "un-built." A data center that was ALREADY fully built and operational before the BEFORE window shows no change (high built-up index before and after) and is silently counted as "un-built" evidence — inverting the meaning. The scorecard nonetheless asserts "MAJORITY of announced capacity is un-built" and "most announced sites have no visible ground footprint" (lines 124, 131-134, 140-141). There is NO caveat anywhere for pre-existing/brownfield/operational sites (grep confirms none in satellite.py or the scorecard); the only caveat is for cloud/seasonal noise. So a real confound (finished-before-observation = "un-built") is presented as fact.

(2) THE 50% LINE IS NOT FIRST-PRINCIPLES — IT IS THE VERY KIND OF BORROWED CUTOFF THE MODULE CLAIMS TO REJECT. The module's stated discipline (docstring lines 3-9; note lines 184-192) is to apply a tipping line "ONLY where a FIRST-PRINCIPLES economic line exists" and to refuse "unvalidated guesses." Duration (debt outlives collateral) and concentration (>50% customer = majority of revenue) genuinely satisfy that bar. But "more than 50% of sites show no change" has no economic mechanism distinguishing 50.1% from 49.9% — it is an arbitrary majority-vote cutoff on a noisy remote-sensing proxy, i.e. exactly the borrowed-threshold style the module purports to reject, relabeled "first-principles_condition."

(3) RAZOR-THIN MARGIN ON AN EXPLICITLY NOISY SIGNAL. In the canonical scenario (test line 27, 48) it clears by only 3.4 points (407/762 = 53.4% vs 50%), while the `mixed_or_minor_change` bucket is excluded from the "no construction" count and satellite.py:137 explicitly warns cloud/seasonal noise can blur the signal. A single-digit reclassification flips the condition, turning "3 of 3" into "2 of 3."

The rest of the claim holds: duration (48mo>24mo) and concentration (CoreWeave ~67%>50%) are sound first-principles lines, and the recourse (72.7% parent-recourse) and tail-size (4.3% leveraged) sub-claims genuinely contradict an SPV-contagion/ecosystem-wide pessimistic framework. So the claim is mostly right, but "3 of the defensible first-principles tipping conditions are met" is an over-claim — the third is a confounded, sub-50%-fragile proxy that is not actually first-principles.
confirmed_weaknesses.recommendation: Adopt the attacker's fix on the execution leg. I independently verified all three technical legs. (1) CONFOUND IS REAL AND UNCAVEATED: classify_construction (satellite.py:64) defines no_significant_change purely as |NDVI/NDBI/BSI delta| < 0.05, with no requirement that the BEFORE state be greenfield. I simulated an already-built/operational site (high built-up index in BOTH the 2023-24 and 2025-26 windows, near-zero deltas) and it classifies as no_significant_change, so it is silently counted into no_change_sites (satellite.py:114-115) which the scorecard relabels 'un-built' / 'no visible ground footprint' as FACT (lines 124,131-134,139-141). The *_before indices are computed (satellite.py:53-54) but never used to gate for greenfield status. grep confirms NO brownfield/operational/already-built caveat anywhere; the only caveat is cloud/seasonal noise. (3) MARGIN IS RAZOR-THIN: 407/762 = 53.4%, clearing the 50% line by only 3.4 points; ~26 reclassifications out of 762 (or shifting mixed_or_minor_change boundary cases) flip the condition, on a signal the module itself flags as noisy. confirmed_weaknesses.weakness:
The betweenness half of the claim survives scrutiny (Amazon Energy 161, Microsoft Energy 112 dominate; CoreWeave is rank-5 at betweenness 13.0 per handoff lines 172-289), but the "Louvain modularity 0.76 confirms the AI cluster is topologically bounded" half is unsupported on two grounds, and that is the strongest real flaw.

(1) DEGENERATE GRAPH -> MODULARITY IS A SPARSITY ARTIFACT. The ai_infra subgraph is 216 nodes / 232 edges (handoff lines 170-171): average degree ~2.15, only 16 edges beyond a spanning forest. This is a near-tree, not a connected network. High Louvain modularity (0.7574) on a sparse near-acyclic graph is essentially automatic — sparse forests partition into high-modularity blocks trivially, and modularity on such graphs is governed by sparsity and the known resolution limit, not by cohesive cluster structure. 28 communities over 216 nodes (~8 nodes each) is consistent with weakly-connected fragments. Yet gds_graph_analytics.py line 41 sets _STRONG_MODULARITY = 0.5 and lines 103-104 assert "high modularity means the network is genuinely community-structured, not a hairball" — treating 0.76 as substantive when on a 232-edge near-forest it carries almost no information about boundedness.

(2) CIRCULAR CROSS-VALIDATION. The subgraph is DEFINED by the filter WHERE r.ai_infra = true (scripts/gds_analytics.py line 36). Louvain runs only on that pre-selected subset. So lines 105-106 of gds_graph_analytics.py claiming the boundedness read is "independent of the entity map and the capture-recapture estimate" is false: the subgraph membership IS the entity map / ai_infra classification. Modularity computed inside a hand-imposed boundary cannot independently confirm that the boundary is real.

Supporting signal of an unreliable substrate: the full-graph PageRank "systemic importance" list (handoff lines 122-149) ranks extraction-noise nodes ("Restriction on Stock Repurchases . So long", "Capital Stock . So long", "Distributions on Capital Stock") ABOVE real banks like JPMCB — the node table contains covenant-text fragments as entities, eroding confidence in any topology-derived inference.</weakness>
<parameter name="suggested_fix">Split the claim. Keep the betweenness finding as stated (energy intermediaries are the structural chokepoints; CoreWeave rank-5) — it holds. Drop or heavily caveat the modularity inference: replace "modularity 0.76 confirms the AI cluster is topologically bounded" with "the ai_infra subgraph is a 232-edge near-forest (avg degree 2.15), so its 0.76 modularity is largely a sparsity artifact and the high value is expected for any sparse graph; it does not independently confirm boundedness because the subgraph boundary was pre-imposed by the ai_infra filter." In gds_graph_analytics.py, (a) remove the "independent of the entity map" / "cross-validates" language on lines 104-106 since the partition is run inside a pre-filtered subgraph, (b) report graph density / edge-to-node ratio alongside modularity and gate the "strongly_modular" flag on a sparsity-aware baseline (e.g., compare to modularity of a degree-matched random/configuration-model graph) rather than a flat 0.5 threshold, and (c) flag that the full-graph node table contains covenant-text extraction noise before drawing topology conclusions.</suggested_fix>
</invoke>

confirmed_weaknesses.weakness: The "~$25.1B debt at risk" is CoreWeave's ENTIRE total debt (handoffs/ai_direct_debt_census_20260603.json: "total_debt_usd": 25149000000), and propagate_shock attributes 100% of a directly-hit issuer's debt to ANY single counterparty that touches it, with no apportionment by that counterparty's actual share of the issuer. See src/bubble/analysis/contagion_propagation.py:71 — debt_at_risk = round(sum(graph["debt_by_issuer"].get(i, 0.0) for i in directly_hit), 2) — debt_by_issuer holds the issuer's full census total (debt_census.py:88), and the build loop (lines 39-53) adds an edge for every customer with no revenue-share weighting (grep confirms no concentration/share/pct term in the file). The over-attribution is concrete: CoreWeave's DOMINANT offtaker is Microsoft at 67% of FY2025 revenue (contagion edges JSON line 8), not OpenAI; OpenAI is one of three named customers (~$18.4B cumulative multi-year commitment = $6.5B + $11.9B through 2030/2031, JSON line 14) and Meta is ~$14.2B (line 20). The engine would emit the identical "$25.1B at risk" for a Microsoft-only OR Meta-only OR OpenAI-only failure, because each is just one edge to CoreWeave. So the claim's causal wording ("OpenAI fails -> ~$25.1B at risk at CoreWeave") treats a partial-offtaker withdrawal as wiping out CoreWeave's entire debt-servicing base, when the largest revenue source (Microsoft) and a second large committed offtaker (Meta) would remain. The in-code note (lines 121-127) caveats only "an upper bound ... not a probability-weighted loss" — that addresses default probability, NOT the attribution error of crediting one ~1/3-of-backlog customer with 100% of the debt. Severity is material not fatal: directionality is sound (OpenAI is the flagged capital-markets-dependent/fragile node, CoreWeave is genuinely exposed, real propagation to lenders/NVIDIA/co-customers exists) and the figure is honestly labeled an upper bound in code; but the headline number is mis-scoped.
confirmed_weaknesses.recommendation:
Confirm the weakness and apply suggested-fix (a)+(c); reject the attacker's "identical output across offtakers" illustration as factually wrong, but the underlying over-attribution is real and material.

WHAT I VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY:

The edge-build loop (lines 39-53) adds one edge per customer with no revenue/share weight; grep for concentration|revenue.?share|apportion|pct in the file returns nothing (exit 1).
- The OpenAI->$25.1B figure IS reader-facing. I generated the emitted node: origin="OpenAI", directly_hit_issuers=["CoreWeave"], debt_at_risk_usd=25149000000.0. It is stored at mismatch_ratios.demand_funding_durability.fragile_demand_failure_cascade (generate_final_burry_report.py:2960-2967) and the whole report dict is serialized to JSON at line 4723. So the bare "OpenAI withdraws -> $25.1B at CoreWeave" is emitted with no surviving-offtaker / Microsoft-67% context on the node.
- Caveat scope CONFIRMED as inadequate to this point. The only caveats — the engine note ("upper bound ... not a probability-weighted loss", lines 125-126) and trigger_basis ("NOT a probability, an upper-bound directly-exposed leverage if that demand withdraws", lines 2962-2964) — address default PROBABILITY, not the ATTRIBUTION error of crediting a ~1/3-of-backlog customer with 100% of the issuer's debt. WHERE THE ATTACKER OVERREACHED (two factual errors, do not adopt this reasoning verbatim):
- FALSE: "The engine would emit the identical $25.1B for a Microsoft-only OR Meta-only OR OpenAI-only failure, because each is just one edge to CoreWeave." I ran it: Microsoft hits CoreWeave+IREN+Nebius = $33.22B; Meta hits CoreWeave+Nebius = $29.26B; OpenAI hits CoreWeave alone = $25.15B. They are NOT identical, and Microsoft/Meta are NOT single-edge-to-CoreWeave nodes — the cross-issuer breadth dimension does differentiate them. The over-attribution is real WITHIN an issuer, not "identical across offtakers."

confirmed_weaknesses.weakness: The causal claim — "a moderate (not tail) demand/financing shock PUSHES the core into distress" — is false on the model's own source-backed data. Running stress_cluster on the 11-issuer fixture (handoffs/ai_direct_issuer_financials_20260602.json) gives breach counts of base=7/11, adverse=8/11, severe=10/11, tail=10/11. A MAJORITY (7 of 11) already breaches at the BASE scenario, which has utilization_miss=0, rate_shock_bps=0, depr_accel=0 (scenario_stress.py:20) — i.e., ZERO shock applied. Seven issuers (WULF, APLD, HUT, MARA, NBIS, CORZ, CIFR) carry negative EBITDA in the unstressed source financials, so they breach on the EBITDA<0 leg regardless of any stress. The "first majority breach at adverse" headline is an artifact of line 98, which hard-excludes base from the majority search (`s["scenario"] != "base"`); without that exclusion the first-majority-breach scenario is base itself. The adverse shock incrementally pushes only ONE additional issuer into breach (7→8), so the shock does not "push the core into distress" — the core is already in distress before any shock. The breach metric also conflates two very different states: a coverage<1 liquidity squeeze vs. structurally negative operating EBITDA. Counting an issuer that is already EBITDA-negative at base as "pushed into distress by a moderate non-tail shock" (the exact framing in the code note at scenario_stress.py:111-112 and in the report at generate_final_burry_report.py:1893-1895) is a logical/labeling error: it attributes a pre-existing condition to the stress scenario. The "thin buffer... majority breach by the adverse case" narrative therefore misstates what the model shows; the true finding is the stronger but differently-shaped statement "a majority are ALREADY non-viable (negative EBITDA) at base, and the cluster aggregate coverage flips negative under a moderate shock."
confirmed_weaknesses.recommendation: Fix the causal/labeling defect; do not retract the finding (corrected version is stronger). I independently re-ran stress_cluster on the source fixture (handoffs/ai_direct_issuer_financials_20260602.json, mapped exactly as scripts/generate_final_burry_report.py:2687-2698 does) and reproduced the attacker's numbers exactly: breach counts base=7/11, adverse=8/11, severe=10/11, tail=10/11; cluster coverage 1.35x (base) -> -0.24x (adverse). The 7 base breachers (WULF, APLD, HUT, MARA, NBIS, CORZ, CIFR) ALL carry negative source EBITDA and breach on the stressed_ebitda<0 leg at zero shock (scenario_stress.py:20 has all-zero base params). The adverse shock adds exactly ONE issuer (CoreWeave), so "the count of the financed cluster PUSHED into distress by a moderate, non-tail shock" (generate_final_burry_report.py:1893-1895) and the note "majority breach by the adverse case" (scenario_stress.py:111-112) misattribute a pre-existing condition to the scenario. Line 98 (`and s["scenario"] != "base"`) is what manufactures the "first majority breach = adverse" headline; without it the honest first-majority scenario is base. CONFIRMED material weakness. Apply the attacker's fix: (1) report that a majority (7/11) are already non-viable (negative operating EBITDA) at base before any shock; (2) state the shock's marginal effect separately (adds ~1 issuer; flips aggregate cluster coverage from +1.35x to -0.24x); (3) split the single breaches flag (scenario_stress.py:57) into a coverage<1 liquidity breach vs a negative-EBITDA non-viability flag; (4) stop labeling already-EBITDA-negative issuers as "pushed into distress" by the scenario. Reject only the attacker's "fatal" grade: no data is fabricated, every figure is source-backed and correct, and the corrected statement ("a majority are already non-viable at base; a moderate shock flips cluster coverage negative") is at least as damning as the original, so the forensic signal survives intact -- the defect is in the causal narrative/labeling, which is material, not fatal.
